wallpapers.title: FERN STAR
wallpapers.line1: Wilson Bentley of Jericho, Vermont, photographed his first snowflake on 15 January 1885.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: HEXAGONAL PLATE
wallpapers.line1: Snowflakes have six sides because of the hexagonal crystal structure of ice.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: TRIANGLE
wallpapers.line1: A three-sided crystal. A snowflake's shape is set by the temperature and humidity of the air it grows in.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: NEEDLE STAR
wallpapers.line1: Bentley caught each crystal on a blackboard and moved it fast to a microscope slide, under a bellows camera.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: SIX PETALS
wallpapers.line1: Bentley took more than 5,000 pictures of snow crystals in his life.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: BRANCHED STAR
wallpapers.line1: Six branching arms, called dendrites, grown out from a tiny hexagon at the centre.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: HEXAGON
wallpapers.line1: Bentley argued that no two snow crystals were alike.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: SIX-POINTED STAR
wallpapers.line1: Known as Snowflake Bentley, he was born in Jericho, Vermont, in 1865 and died in 1931.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: RIBBED PLATE
wallpapers.line1: A flat plate, one of the basic shapes of snow, with ribs running out to each of its six sides.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: STAR AND HEXAGON
wallpapers.line1: Each of these prints, on gelatin silver paper, is only about 7 cm across.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: PLATE WITH ARMS
wallpapers.line1: A plate at the centre, with short broad arms grown from its corners.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)

wallpapers.title: BROAD-ARMED STAR
wallpapers.line1: The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York bought these prints in 2015 and shares them free for any use.
wallpapers.line2: 1890s–1920s  ·  Photo: Wilson A. Bentley  ·  The Met, public domain (CC0)
